B2.v: VALIDATION — MODEL AGAINST 17 ACTUAL PURCHASE ORDERS

B3.v: Source: PO_details April 2021 to date, PO Data Bank tab. Model run once per PO on that PO's rating, emission norm and engine make, with acoustic enclosure and AMF panel held constant. Duty set to Standby throughout — see finding 1. Two model columns are shown: at Market price stance and at the Should-cost target stance, which is the workbook default.

L9.v: 6.6 kV HT set — model assumes 415 V

B23.v: Mean signed variance to PO, should-cost stance

B29.v: The model is now a should-cost floor, not a market price

B30.v: The Pricing stance input on the Inputs tab drives the whole commercial block. Market price reproduces a dealer-supplied set at prevailing terms. Should-cost target — the workbook default — assumes TPL buys direct rather than through an integrator, negotiates the engine at 8% and the alternator at 6% on volume, and holds the builder to a 5% margin on a 4.5% overhead. Aggressive floor is the walk-away. Nothing in the physical build-up was changed to achieve this.

B31.v: At should-cost the model sits below 13 of 17 POs, averaging 7.1% under

B32.v: At the Market stance it sat above 13 of 17 and averaged 10.8% over. The Aggressive floor clears 15 of 17 and averages 12.2% under. Sitting below every single PO would need a 30% cut, which no build-up supports and which would put the model 30% under the ten POs it already beats.

B33.v: The four POs the model cannot get under are the ones worth studying

B34.v: 250 and 320 kVA from Powerica, 500 kVA from Sudhir and 650 kVA from Goel. Two of them clear at the Aggressive floor. The Powerica pair do not, at any defensible stance.

B35.v: The CPCB IV+ premium is measured, and the model's estimate holds

B36.v: Same vendor, same rating, five months apart: 250 kVA Sudhir standby moved from Rs 7,796/kVA on CPCB II to Rs 10,102/kVA on CPCB IV+, a premium of 29.6%. The model assumes 32%. The largest unquoted assumption in the workbook now has evidence behind it.

B37.v: The Powerica prices are a bundled allocation, not a standalone rate

B38.v: PO 5700035672 covers 250, 320 and 625 kVA in one order. The 250 and 320 lines are the cheapest in the whole bank, while the 625 line at Rs 9,089/kVA sits 9.6% ABOVE Goel's 650 kVA set on the same norm. Price has been moved between lines inside the package. Chasing the 250 and 320 rates in isolation will not reproduce them.

B39.v: Duty label tracks the vendor, not the machine

B40.v: Every prime-labelled PO came from one vendor, and at 250 and 320 kVA the prime set is the cheapest of three — the opposite of what a genuine prime rating costs. All 17 are therefore run at nameplate, with duty treated as a specification note.

B41.v: Two POs, same rating, same vendor, same day, 10.8% apart

B42.v: 910 kVA CPCB II from Sudhir Power appears twice on 29-Mar-2024 at Rs 7,286 and Rs 8,075 per kVA. The second records an AMF panel and the first does not. Worth confirming a panel is worth Rs 7.2 lakh on a 910 kVA set.
